newsitem.title: GERMANY: German state in legal move to block 'maglev' train.
newsitem.headline: German state in legal move to block 'maglev' train.

text.p: The state of Schleswig-Holstein in northern Germany said on Tuesday it filed a suit with the Constitutional Court to block construction of the high-speed Transrapid magnetic levitation (maglev) train.

State economics minister Peer Steinbrueck said the law suit challenged a federal law that he alleged violated the rights of property owners who would be forced to allow the Transrapid to cross their property.
Steinbrueck also said the Federal government failed to conduct the usual studies required to determine feasibility of the project or whether it was needed to meet transportation needs in the region.

The Transrapid, a futuristic train that runs on magnetic levitation technology at speeds of over 400 km an hour, is slated to be built in a first pilot project to connect Germany's two largest cities Berlin and Hamburg.

The plan has met stiff opposition from environmental groups and sceptical state politicians who allege that the government based its decision on inaccurate forecasts regarding the costs of the project and traffic requirements.
Opponents of the project have said it would be less expensive to use existing rail technology to create a high-speed connection between the two cities.
The Transrapid is being built by an industry consortium that includes Thyssen AG and Daimler-Benz.
